title: CrossPrefetch: Accelerating I/O Prefetching for Modern Storage
problem: Existing OS prefetching mechanisms have rigid interfaces that lack feedback on prefetch effectiveness, suffer from high concurrency bottlenecks with lock contention, and inefficiently utilize available system memory for prefetch buffers.
motivation: I/O prefetching is critical for storage performance, and current OS-level approaches significantly limit how applications can optimize their access patterns and adapt prefetch strategies.
method: CrossPrefetch divides prefetching responsibilities between the OS kernel and a user-level runtime layer. The OS performs low-level prefetch operations while the runtime provides application feedback on prefetch effectiveness and manages memory allocation for prefetch buffers. This cross-layered design reduces lock contention and synchronization overhead by allowing the runtime to coordinate with applications without kernel barriers.
key_novelty: Cross-layered prefetching architecture that divides responsibilities between OS and user-level runtime to provide prefetch effectiveness feedback while minimizing synchronization overhead.
contributions: Cross-layered I/O prefetching mechanism splitting OS and runtime concerns
Prefetch effectiveness feedback mechanism from OS to applications
Reduced lock contention and concurrency bottlenecks through improved interface design
More efficient system memory utilization for prefetch buffers

metrics.speedup: higher I/O performance (specific numbers not provided in abstract)
metrics.other: reduced cache misses, reduced lock contentions
